summary.headline: Regency Fincorp FY26 PAT rose 170% to INR13.4 crore on AUM of INR261.2 crore (up 45%), with secured MSME now about 61% of AUM.
summary.overview: Maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) covering AUM, disbursements, profitability and asset quality. Management said the book is shifting from unsecured and JLG microfinance toward secured MSME lending and a planned salaried digital lending product (Cash My Salary app). Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, which management attributed to legacy JLG and short-tenor unsecured loans. Management outlined a target of INR500-550 crore AUM this year and INR3,000 crore by FY30, funded by INR400-450 crore of expected lender borrowings. Cost of funds is currently 13-14%, with a target of 11-12% and a longer-term aim of 10-10.5%.

segments.name: Secured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured share of disbursement rose to about 57% in FY26 from 23% in FY25; secured book is about 61% of AUM versus 18% a year earlier. Average tenure 48-60 months, LTV 50-60%, ROI reducing from 20% to 24%.

segments.name: Unsecured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Book run down from about INR104 crore to about INR60 crore. Tenure around 12 months, kept for cash flow and collection continuity.

segments.name: JLG (group microfinance)
segments.commentary: About 10.5% of AUM. No disbursements since November 2025. Expected about 70% run-down by end FY27 and zero by end of calendar 2027.

segments.name: Digital personal loans (Cash My Salary)
segments.commentary: Salaried borrowers earning above INR45,000; pilot live with approval in 30-45 minutes; priced at about 24% flat for a six-month tenor. Targeted at 15-20% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of about INR500-550 crore this year, roughly doubling from INR261 crore, with about 80% secured MSME, about INR75-100 crore digital, and INR400 crore secured.
Branch network to roughly double to about 50 branches by end FY27 and mid-calendar 2027, from 23 currently.
Cost of funds target of 11-12% this year (from 13-14%), with a further goal of 10-10.5% within 12 months; 10.25% cited for a net cost of funds.
Opex expected at about 2-2.75% of AUM; lending rates expected at 15-16% after cost reductions.
AUM target of INR3,000 crore by FY30.
NIM expected to be maintained at current levels rather than increased; PPI licence approval expected in the coming quarter or financial year.
capex_capacity: 23 branches; average branch AUM about INR10-12 crore (range from INR3 crore to INR10 crore).
Branches capable of disbursing about INR2-2.5 crore per month on average.
Plan to raise INR400-450 crore from banks and NBFCs this year, including ICICI, Axis, Yes Bank, LC Venture Debt, Lighthouse Canton and others.
RBI NOC received for PPI licence; digital wallet RedPay to launch within 12 months.
INR25 crore raised via compulsorily convertible debentures in April 2026, to fund secured MSME growth and digital lending.
demand_pricing: Average MSME ticket size INR35-45 lakh; collateral is residential or commercial constructed property (no land, industrial land or agri land), with an LTV of 50-60%.
Lending is restricted to non-trading MSMEs (hardware, small restaurants, hotels, small manufacturers); no real estate or trading lending.
Collection efficiency about 95-96% on zero-month basis and 97-98% on zero-plus basis.
Zero-plus DPD about INR2.2 crore (under 1% of AUM); 90-day PAR about INR65-70 lakh per the Q&A answer, and about INR40-60 lakh in another answer.
Expansion focus remains North India (Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, NCR); West India is next and South is not planned for 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What collateral secures the MSME loans and what is the SARFAESI and recovery process?
qa_highlights.answer: Collateral is mainly residential or commercial property at 50-60% LTV, with an average collateral value of INR65-75 lakh. Only one 90-DPD secured account is in legal recovery, expected to be liquidated within the quarter; in-house lawyers handle notices and third parties handle recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How will AUM reach INR500-550 crore and then INR3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to run down the unsecured book, raise INR400-450 crore from lenders, double branches to about 50, and keep opex at 2.5-2.75%. It targets INR3,000 crore AUM by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How are NIMs protected as the mix shifts to secured lending, and what is the cost of funds target?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM is about 10.75-11% and is expected to hold at current levels as the digital product at about 24% offsets lower MSME yields. Cost of funds is 13-14% today, targeted at 11-12%, with a further decline possible once public sector banks lend.

qa_highlights.question: What drives asset quality deterioration and is the NPA rise structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA rise to legacy JLG and Karja Mukti Abhiyan stress in Punjab and Haryana, plus short-tenor loans. It said the secured salaried book is less risky and cited industry NPA of about 1.5-1.6% versus its 0.76%.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates the company and how does the PPI licence help?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sources 100% of leads in-house with no DSA, and the PPI wallet will give bank-statement visibility for early risk signals and cheaper lead generation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost of funds fall to 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to 8%, saying it expects a significant reduction in cost of funds and would pass part of the 2% arbitrage to customers within 12 months.

risks_watch: Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, and the secured book is still seasoning; watch 90-DPD and collections in the secured book.
Heavy dependence on borrowings (INR400-450 crore planned) and a high cost of funds of 13-14%; rate cuts are targeted but not yet achieved.
Asset-liability tenor matching depends on borrowings of 4-5 years matching 48-60 month loans.
Regulatory approval of the PPI licence and the scale-up of Cash My Salary are still pending.
Concentration in North India, a region the company itself described as having delinquency-prone segments; the JLG run-down is still ongoing.
Disclosure inconsistencies on 90-DPD and CRAR prior-year figures; verify against the audited financial statements.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on strategy, with specific numbers on secured mix and cost targets. Answers on asset quality and forward cost of funds were more hedged, and some figures (PAR, CRAR trend) were given inconsistently.
key_quotes: Our approach has been to operate in these spaces with a model that is high yield, but tightly controlled. Because in lending, growth without discipline does not last.
The shift is deliberate strategy move to build a more resilient and low risk portfolio.
We will only have two products which has been focused for our company, which is MSME secured lending and digital lending part of it.
We are not doing any lending to any trading company, no real estate, no trading.

down YoY per analyst question; no prior figure stated

growth.why: Management guides AUM to INR500-550 crore this year (roughly doubling from INR261 crore) and a branch network from 23 to about 50 by FY27 end, backed by INR400-450 crore of planned lender borrowings and INR25 crore of CCDs raised in April 2026, though no specific branch-level capex was given.
